body:
Credit @MDX-Tom for the report and both captures. Verified against the current code (`d8b3749ef`) with both of your captures in hand. The observations are real, and this issue is right about *where* to look — but on this route magpie is not dropping citation data that upstream gives it: **the googleSearch grounding payload on this route carries no quotable page text**, so there is nothing honest to put in `cited_text`. The fix this issue proposes has to manufacture it, and that is exactly the pattern the maintainer rejected when closing plugins#656. Breakdown:

## 1. Where the citations die on this route — two seats

Routing first: `antigravity/*` is a Google sign-in served on Code Assist. With a function tool declared (as DSH's translated request has), Antigravity turns its own googleSearch down (400, `include_server_side_tool_invocations`), so magpie runs the search for the model with the account itself — `searchRank`'s `googleAccount(p)` case, googleSearch on Code Assist (`internal/gateway/search.go`). Your experiment 2 changed the *answered* model, not the searcher: the searcher is a global setting, so both captures went through the same Vertex grounding backend — which is why the free-model route behaved identically.

**Seat 1 — no excerpt exists to cite.** The Code Assist decoder reads googleSearch's `groundingMetadata` and keeps `groundingChunks[].web.{uri,title}` (`internal/gateway/codeassist.go`) — that is all this grounding shape carries per page: a redirect address and a title, which your captures show (`vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/...`, bare-domain titles, `encrypted_content: ""`). Google's documented googleSearch grounding carries no page text in `groundingChunks`; the only free-text field in the whole payload is `groundingSupports[].segment.text`, and the API documents that as a span of **the model's own answer** mapped to the chunk indices — not the page's text. So `Hit.Cited` is `""` for every hit on this route.

**Seat 2 — the model named no URL.** Since 1d6b72ad (#3447), the text after a search is cut into lines, and a line that names a found page's URL whole becomes its own text block with that page's `web_search_result_location` citations (`internal/gateway/search_cite.go`, `citesOf`). Your captures' text blocks are prose with site names — no URLs at all — so no line qualifies and no citation block is made. (The web_search tool's prompt does ask the model to cite the URLs it uses; gemini-3.8-flash just didn't.) Note that even a URL-naming line would not have helped DSH on this route: `cited_text` is `Hit.Cited` clipped to 150 (`""` here), and DSH's `citationSnippets` requires `cite.url && cite.cited_text`. The stream shows no `citations_delta` for the same reason — the streamed path emits exactly the citations the whole reply carries (`sayCited`), and none exist.

## 2. Why the proposed fix crosses the line

Building `web_search_result_location` entries whose `cited_text` comes from groundingSupports segments — or any model output — presents the model's words as the source page's text. That is verbatim the pattern yetone rejected when closing plugins#656 («新的 cited_text 不是网页内容，而是模型自己的回答…这等于把模型的话当成来源原文展示给用户» — *the new cited_text is not the page's content but the model's own answer; it presents the model's words as the source's original text*), a review this issue itself endorses as "完全中肯且专业". magpie has held one rule since #3447: **a page nothing was quoted of gets no citation — none is invented.** On this route Google quotes nothing, so magpie writes no citations — the same decision that correctly leaves DeepSeek's sealed results citation-free (route B in #3447's verification). This is a data-availability boundary at the upstream protocol, not a gap in the Anthropic translation layer; #3447's face is alive wherever excerpts exist (search APIs' page text, Anthropic searchers' own `cited_text` — verified on 0.1.1371 in that issue), and your middleware PoC is the proof from the other side: the client lights up the moment *real* citations exist.

## 3. What would make this fixable in core

- **Raw grounding bytes.** The captures here are the client-facing Anthropic shape — post-translation. If a capture of magpie's own upstream Code Assist stream on this route shows a field carrying source-page text (beyond `uri`/`title`), attach it here: core can carry it the way `Hit.Cited` already does, and that becomes an ordinary patch (streamed and whole). This is the same raw-bytes ask the plugins#656 review made.
- **A searcher whose API returns page text.** magpie's search-API searchers already carry page text into `cited_text` (`search_api.go`); pointing the Searcher setting at one of those gets DSH live snippets today, without touching magpie. (Vertex AI Search data-store grounding returns `retrievedContext.text`, but that is a different product than the account's googleSearch.)

Until one of those holds, the honest answer on this route is the one magpie gives: results with titles and addresses, and text without citations.

AI use: analysis written with GLM-5.3-Flash (ZCode) from a code read of the repo; no requests were sent to any upstream.
